name: Château de la Négly Coteaux du Languedoc La Clape Porte du Ciel 2016
text:
## Château de la Négly La Clape Porte du Ciel 2016

**Story.** The estate sits on the [Massif de la Clape](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Massif+de+la+Clape,+Narbonne,+France&t=k) near [Narbonne](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Narbonne,+France&t=k). [Château de la Négly](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Chateau+de+la+Negly,+Narbonne,+France&t=k) was called Ancely in the 18th century, renamed Nerly in 1781 and La Négly in 1807. The Paux-Rosset family replanted it to Syrah, Grenache and Mourvèdre. The estate vineyard is clay-limestone, and the neighbouring Boède vineyard is sandy-loam and sandstone.

**Reviews.** The 2016 has the strongest professional support on your list after the Grand Veneur. The Wine Advocate (Joe Czerwinski, May 2019) gave it 97. Jeb Dunnuck gave it 99, which I confirmed on his site. Falstaff (Peter Moser, 2020) gave it 98. CellarTracker community score, from your list: 95.5 (2016).

**Practical note.** Czerwinski suggested a couple of years' wait, then 15+ years of drinking, so it is in its window now. Decant for an hour. Grilled lamb chops or a cassoulet would do it justice.

**Curious aside: an island turned limestone.** The massif is Lower Cretaceous limestone, karst, with about 600 mm of rain a year. It was an island in Roman times and was joined to the mainland later by silt from the Aude river.

### From the history books
- 1316: a flood shifts the Aude's course north of the massif (see [La Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- 1807: the estate takes the name La Négly, as above. See [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Narbonne&go=Go).
- From 1863: while phylloxera spread through France, the Massif de la Clape went unaffected. See [Great French Wine Blight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_French_Wine_Blight).

**Sources:** Jeb Dunnuck (subscriber site, checked directly), Uncorked, Falstaff, Farr Vintners, J.J. Buckley, Vinfolio, FRW, First Bottle, Kysela, Benchmark Wine, K&L, Whwc, Thatchers, Winewithseth, CellarTracker, Delectable, closdesspiritueux.com, and Wikipedia ([Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC), [Nahe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahe_(wine_region)), [Vouvray AOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vouvray_AOC), [La Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape), [Avignon Papacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy), [Great French Wine Blight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_French_Wine_Blight)).
